LESSON: READING POSTURE

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 3.6: Reading Posture

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading Posture. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Identify correct reading poems and rhymes related to appropriate reading postures in pictures or in class. posture
2. Identify incorrect reading • Learners could be exposed to models of correct postures in pictures or in class. reading posture

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Identify correct reading poems and rhymes related to appropriate reading postures in pictures or in class. posture
   In simple words: practise until you can identify correct reading poems and rhymes related to appropriate reading postures in pictures or in class. posture. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. Identify incorrect reading • Learners could be exposed to models of correct postures in pictures or in class. reading posture
   In simple words: practise until you can identify incorrect reading • Learners could be exposed to models of correct postures in pictures or in class. reading posture. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading Posture using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading Posture in the examples.
2. Explain Reading Posture to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading Posture.
4. Show that you can: Identify correct reading poems and rhymes related to appropriate reading postures in pictures or in class. posture

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading Posture using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading Posture important for a PP1 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Be exposed to models of correct postures in pictures or in class. reading posture. d) Enjoy participating in reading

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Identify correct reading poems and rhymes related to appropriate reading postures in pictures or in class. posture
